name: Cite Religieuse (The Cliff Village)
tagline: Chapels and sanctuaries carved into the cliff face
description: The heart of Rocamadour, where seven chapels, the Black Madonna sanctuary and pilgrim stairways cling directly to the limestone cliff above the Alzou gorge. It is stunning, deeply atmospheric and packed with day visitors for much of the year. Practically no long-term housing exists here, and mobility is a real factor given the steps.
pros: Walkable to chapels, shops and cafes
cons: Overwhelmed by tour groups in season

name: Chateau Plateau (Upper Town)
tagline: Clifftop chateau with sweeping gorge views
description: Perched at the very top of the cliff above the sanctuary, this small cluster around the restored chateau offers the best panoramic views of the gorge and countryside. Reached via the Stations of the Cross path or an elevator, it is quieter than the lower village and feels more residential, though options remain very limited.
pros: Far quieter than the lower village
Access to ramparts and walking paths
cons: Requires climbing or the elevator to reach

name: L'Hospitalet
tagline: The practical base just above the gorge
description: A small settlement on the plateau above Rocamadour, historically a rest stop for pilgrims and now the most practical base for visitors, with hotels, gites, parking and a viewpoint over the entire cliff village. It has easier road access and a calmer pace than the village below, while still being a short walk or drive from the sanctuary.
pros: Iconic viewpoint over the cliff village
cons: Less atmospheric than the medieval core
Still limited dining and no coworking

name: Gramat
tagline: A real working town fifteen minutes away
description: The nearest proper town, about fifteen minutes by car, with a weekly market, supermarkets, everyday cafes and better connectivity than Rocamadour itself. It lacks the drama of the cliff village but offers a far more livable base for anyone staying in the area for weeks rather than days, with easy driving access to Rocamadour and Padirac.
bestFor: longer stays, remote work, groceries and errands
cons: No cliffside charm or major sights
Still requires a car for most trips
